songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Searing Dark Star and fiery Morning Dew despite muddy tape
ai_show_review.blurb: The set kicks off with a blistering Morning Dew that rolls straight into an expansive Dark Star where Jerry’s guitar burns and Mickey Hart supplies a solo‑driven groove. Turn On Your Lovelight lifts the second half, and New Potato Caboose adds a rare moment of early‑'68 charm, though the organ is almost inaudible.
ai_show_review.review: Columbus Veterans Hall on November 22, 1968 captures the Dead at a pivotal late‑summer point. Even though both surviving recordings are audience tapes with the usual ’68 hiss and mud, the performance shines through. Jerry Garcia’s guitar is described as “searing‑hot” and a “snarling beast,” especially on Dark Star and Morning Dew, while Mickey Hart’s solo drumming carries the set when Bill Kreutzmann was sidelined by illness. Phil Lesh holds down a solid bass foundation that feels right despite being buried in the mix, and Pigpen’s organ is barely audible but still present. Highlights such as Turn On Your Lovelight gain surprising clarity later in the tape, and the rare New Potato Caboose provides a glimpse of early‑'68 experimentation. Listeners willing to brave the lo‑fi ambience will be rewarded with one of the era’s most intense live moments.

best_recording.reason: Fair‑quality audience tape with a recent remaster that adds warmth, preserving Jerry’s searing guitar and the epic Dark Star while keeping most of the set intact.

key_highlights: Epic Dark Star featuring Mickey Hart’s solo drumming
Turn On Your Lovelight gains surprising clarity in the latter half
Rare New Potato Caboose appears despite faint organ presence

band_performance.Jerry: Searing‑hot, snarling guitar that rips through Dark Star and Morning Dew, delivering both caressing melodies and fierce attacks.
band_performance.Phil: Solid bass foundation that feels right even though the tape muddies his low end; underpins the jams with reliable groove.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ is barely audible on this audience recording; faint presence on tracks like New Potato Caboose, but largely lost in the mix.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums alone for most of the set, delivering powerful straight‑ahead percussion and a standout solo that defines the show’s unique feel.
band_performance.Billy: Absent due to illness for part of the night; when present his playing is masked by poor tape quality, leaving a thinner overall drum texture.
